---
title: "Trump 2.0 tariffs. Part III"
description: "A chaotic four days: tariffs on Canada, China and Mexico trigger swift retaliation, then a stock-market slide forces a partial climbdown within days."
date: "2025-03-07"
categories: [trade-wars]
---

Covers a chaotic four-day stretch, March 3–7, 2025. On March 3, Trump
implemented 25% tariffs on Canada, China, and Mexico, drawing immediate
retaliation: China hit $21 billion of US agricultural exports, Canada
announced $155 billion in countermeasures. After the resulting market
turbulence wiped out post-election gains, Trump backed down by March 6,
delaying tariffs until April 2 for USMCA-compliant goods and exempting
roughly half of Mexican and 62% of Canadian imports. The piece calls the
episode "a mess that destroys the credibility" of the policy, noting that odd
additions like potash to the tariff list look driven by specific lobbying
rather than strategy.

**Originally published on Substack**, March 7, 2025.
